text:
One: write a constitution and have every member sign it: how much everyone pays and by when, what happens if someone falls behind or wants to leave, who the chairperson and treasurer are, and how and when the money is paid out. You don't have to start from scratch: NASASA has templates. Two: open a separate stokvel bank account, and never keep the group's money in one member's personal account. Three: make sure no single person can take money out. Warren Ingram's advice: at least two of three signatories must approve every payment.

Full guide: "Stokvels Explained: How to Protect Your Stokvel Money (South Africa 2026)" on the Money From Zero channel.
